Estimate an unregularized Ising network for binary items

Source: R/ising_unreg.R
ising_sampler.Rd

ising_sampler() estimates an unregularized Ising network from binary items, in which edges can be kept or removed by their statistical significance rather than by a penalty. The Ising model describes binary items through a threshold for each item and an interaction for each pair, the association between two items after conditioning on all others (van Borkulo et al., 2014); estimated without a penalty, the interactions are maximum-likelihood estimates, not shrunk toward zero.

The function regresses each item on all other items by ordinary (unpenalized) logistic regression. With alpha, every coefficient whose Wald p-value, optionally adjusted for multiplicity, exceeds alpha is set to zero. Every pair is estimated twice, once in each item's regression; the AND rule (default) keeps an edge when both estimates remain nonzero, the OR rule when either does, and the edge weight is the mean of the two. The certificate is the largest violation of the maximum-likelihood optimality conditions (the score equations) across the regressions, so a value near zero shows that every regression is at its maximum. Pruning sets coefficients to zero after fitting, without refitting; the pruned network is no longer the solution that was checked, and its certificate is reported as missing.

The result is an undirected network of class psychnet (psychnet).

Unpenalized estimates need many more observations than items. When an item is perfectly predicted by the others (separation), its maximum-likelihood estimate does not exist; the penalized ising_fit() is the alternative then, and in small samples generally.

Usage

ising_sampler(
  data,
  rule = c("AND", "OR"),
  alpha = NULL,
  adjust = "none",
  min_sum = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  na_method = c("pairwise", "listwise"),
  labels = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Binary data: a data frame or matrix with one row per observation, with numeric 0/1, logical, or two-level factor columns, as in ising_fit(). A constant column is dropped.

rule

"AND" (default) keeps an edge when both nodewise estimates are nonzero; "OR" when either is.

alpha

Significance level for pruning, a number in (0, 1). Default NULL keeps every edge.

adjust

Multiplicity correction for the p-values used in pruning, one of stats::p.adjust.methods. Default "none". Used only with alpha.

min_sum

Minimum number of endorsed items per row; rows below it are dropped before fitting. Default NULL keeps every row.

weights

Optional non-negative observation weights, one per row after missing-data handling (and filtered with min_sum). Only their relative sizes matter. Default NULL (unweighted).

na_method

"pairwise" (default) fills each missing value with the item's more frequent value; "listwise" drops rows with a missing value.

labels

Optional node labels: one per node, or one per input column.

Value

An undirected network of class psychnet (psychnet). as.data.frame() gives one row per edge (from, to, weight), certificate() the maximum-likelihood certificate, and net_predict() the predictability of each node. The certificate is missing when pruning removed a coefficient or when a regression did not converge. The object also stores the node thresholds (thresholds), the unadjusted Wald p-values of the nodewise coefficients (p_values, row = the regressed item), the certificate of the unpruned fit (fit_kkt) and what the certificate refers to (certificate_target: "returned_network", "pre_pruning_fit" or "nonconverged_fit").

Details

Edge weights and thresholds are on the log-odds scale of the 0/1 coding, as in ising_fit(). The multiplicity correction (adjust) is applied over all nodewise coefficients, two per pair, before the AND or OR rule. After pruning, the thresholds are recomputed from the retained coefficients; the remaining coefficients keep their unpruned estimates.

Conditions

psychnet_bad_input when a column is not binary, fewer than two usable columns remain, rule, alpha, adjust, min_sum, weights or labels is invalid, or min_sum removes every row (or every row with positive weight); psychnet_constant_variable (warning) when a constant column is dropped; psychnet_separation (warning) when items are perfectly predicted by the others, so their estimates do not exist; psychnet_no_converge (warning) when a regression fails to converge for another reason; psychnet_singular_information (warning) when an item's Fisher information is singular, so its Wald p-values are unreliable.

References

van Borkulo, C. D., Borsboom, D., Epskamp, S., Blanken, T. F., Boschloo, L., Schoevers, R. A., & Waldorp, L. J. (2014). A new method for constructing networks from binary data. Scientific Reports, 4, 5918. doi:10.1038/srep05918

See also

ising_fit() for the penalized model; dichotomize() to prepare items; certificate() and glm_lasso_kkt() for the optimality check; net_predict(); psychnet() with method = "ising_sampler".

Examples

b <- dichotomize(SRL_GPT)
ising_sampler(b)                 # every edge; certificate near zero
#> <psychnet> ising_sampler network
#>   nodes: 5   edges: 10   (undirected)
#>   optimality (KKT residual): 1.07e-08
pruned <- ising_sampler(b, alpha = 0.05)
as.data.frame(pruned)
#>   from to    weight
#> 1  CSU IV 2.4336970
#> 2  CSU SE 1.9776719
#> 3   IV SE 1.5285878
#> 4  CSU SR 1.7964616
#> 5   IV SR 2.0903313
#> 6   SE SR 0.9333181
certificate(pruned)              # missing: pruning changed the fit
#>          method certificate kind certified
#> 1 ising_sampler          NA  kkt        NA
